routes.label: Separate ordinary pay from extra pay

question: Each day Walter gets \(\$3\) for doing his chores or \(\$5\) for doing them exceptionally well. After \(10\) days of doing his chores daily, Walter has received a total of \(\$36.\) On how many days did Walter do them exceptionally well?
solution:
Start by giving Walter the ordinary \(\$3\) payment for each of the \(10\) days. This accounts for
\[
10\cdot\$3=\$30.
\]
Each exceptional day adds \(\$5-\$3=\$2\) to that amount. Walter received \(\$36-\$30=\$6\) extra, so the number of exceptional days was
\[
\$6\div\$2=\boxed{3}.
\]
This leaves \(7\) ordinary days, and \(7\cdot3+3\cdot5=36\), as required. The answer is \(\boxed{3\text{ days}}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{A}}\).
